item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption assessed agencies’ compliance with the Treasury fraud and corruption control policy and barriers to meeting it.
item.support: The purpose of this publication is to assess compliance with the circular and to identify any barriers that limit compliance.

item.text: Its research combined survey responses from 90 agencies, nine focus groups and analysis of agencies’ control documents.
item.support: To assess compliance with the circular, and to understand the drivers of compliance and non-compliance, the Commission conducted three research activities:

item.text: The Commission reports that most agencies met minimum standards, while managing third parties was the requirement agencies found hardest to meet.
item.support: Having robust third-party management systems was seen to be the most difficult aspect of the circular to achieve.
item.section: Chapter 2: Overview of compliance with the circular

item.text: The Commission advises agencies to improve third-party controls through due diligence, clear responsibilities, staff training and reporting arrangements.
item.support: All agencies should ensure that they implement a variety of controls to reduce third-party fraud and corruption risks

item.quote: The research findings show that many agencies do not consistently apply third-party controls.
